result.title: DiFiT: Distribution-Fidelity-guided Visual Token Pruning for Multimodal Large Language Models
result.summary: Visual token pruning reduces the inference cost of multimodal large language models, but answer accuracy only partly reflects its effect. Pruning can change the probabilities of alternative response tokens even when greedy answers remain correct and unchanged. We compare full and pruned response distributions under shared reference prefixes. Average predictive drift grows with compression on fixed correctly answered samples. Separate analyses associate larger drift with more confidence-decision disagreements and sampling failures. We propose DiFiT (Distribution-Fidelity-guided Token pruning) to learn discrete selection from reference answers and full-token response distributions. Dual-View Distillation matches probabilities across the vocabulary, while answer supervision supports task quality. A learned scorer and differentiable Top-$K$ learn which visual evidence to retain. A multi-budget mask objective supports different retention ratios through one shared ranking over a frozen model. On Qwen2.5-VL-7B, DiFiT reduces sampling-induced negative flips by 30.3% relative to FastV at 10% retention on four-task greedy-correct controls. It preserves 98.74% of baseline performance on MME at 30% retention.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究多模态大模型视觉 token 剪枝引起的回答分布漂移，并提出 DiFiT：以参考答案与全 token 分布进行双视角蒸馏，配合可学习评分器和可微 Top-K 选择保留的视觉证据，并用多预算掩码支持不同保留率。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接涉及视觉证据筛选与压缩造成的信息损失；其将贪心答案正确性与分布漂移、置信决策分歧分开分析，可供核查 LVR 中视觉细节保留、答案是否真正使用保留证据及剪枝对推理稳定性的影响。
